subject: RETURN statement
notes: kb/Work PB348 LANDED, completing kb/Work PB339's five conforming obligations with the sixth. RULE (`--check 14.9.34.4 "according to the rules for the MOVE statement without the CORRESPONDING phrase"` => OK, GR5 b)). FOUR OBLIGATIONS WERE VERIFIED CONFORMING and are unchanged: the same RETURN without INTO runs first, the move sits inside the success arm so an unsuccessful RETURN skips it, the record is available in both places, and item identification happens after the read. THE FIFTH, THE RECORD IS VARYING SIZE, rests on a JUSTIFIED receiver and on nothing else (kb/Work PB722): 'The size of the current record is determined by rules specified for the RECORD clause' (cite.py --check 14.9.34.4 => OK 5) b)) sends the reader to 13.18.43.4 GR16 (--check 13.18.43.4 'the number of bytes in the current record that participate as the sending operands in the implicit MOVE statement is determined by the following conditions' => OK 16)), and a left-justified receiver cannot show it: 14.6.8.5 (--check 'aligned at the leftmost character position in the data item with space fill or truncation to the right' => OK) lands a 6-byte sender and the whole space-padded area on the same characters, so the probe that once claimed the size half (PB348's p11, a PIC X(12) receiver) could not fail. 13.18.32.4 separates them: GR1 (--check 'the leftmost character positions or boolean positions of the sending operand shall be truncated' => OK 1)) keeps the rightmost characters of an over-long sender and GR2 (--check 'the data is aligned at the rightmost character position or boolean position in the data item' => OK 2)) right-aligns a short one. Witness: pb339_into_current_record leg G, RETURN from an SD RECORD IS VARYING 3 TO 20 whose released record is the 8 bytes K01PQRST into PIC X(12) JUSTIFIED RIGHT gives [    K01PQRST]; the whole 20-byte space-padded area is an over-long sender whose rightmost twelve characters are all spaces, and that is what the emitter produced until kb/Work PB339 made the sender a BoundCurrentRecord. The READ twin (GR-14.9.30.4-4) is measured on the same shape, legs A, B and F. THE SIXTH -- 'according to the rules for the MOVE statement' -- was not applied at all: the INTO move was constructed in SortEmitter.EmitReturn, downstream of every bind-time MOVE screen. MEASURED before: `RETURN SF INTO WS-RECV` where WS-RECV is TYPE TA and TA is TYPEDEF STRONG compiled and ran silently, while the identical MOVE written explicitly was refused COBOL1533 (14.9.25.3 SR2 / 8.5.3.3); the READ sibling behaved the same way, which is the two-arm shape. WHAT IS THERE NOW: MoveBinder.BindIntoPhrase binds the move for ALL THREE INTO arms -- the sequential READ, the keyed READ and the RETURN -- because 14.9.30.4 GR4 b) and 14.9.34.4 GR5 b) are the SAME SENTENCE, and it carries PB339's 13.18.43.4 GR16 sender builder with it (an operand is a bind-time object). CheckStrongMove now names the phrase, so the diagnostic reads 'the implicit MOVE of RETURN ... INTO (ISO 14.9.34.4 GR5 b))'. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 . 2002 . 2014 . 2023 retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Validation/StatementValidation.cs#CheckStrongMove (kb/Work PB878 deleted StatementValidation.CheckStrongMove; the RETURN INTO move's MOVE-rule screen is the one MoveTable16.Validity chain, framed by MoveBinder.MoveCategoryLegality)
